correctness.rationale: Because 3 is invertible over Z_(2), the cubic Cartier divisor has a nonzero special reduction and is flat. The substitution ui=Xi+X6 removes the vertex coordinate in characteristic two, giving sum ui^3 with sum ui=0. Its four partial derivatives are (zi+t)^2; the invertible I+J coordinate change and Euler identity give local Jacobian k[w1..w4]/(w1^2,...,w4^2), length 16. The induced nondegenerate four-dimensional Hermitian form gives a smooth cubic surface; its 27 geometric lines correspond to all planes of the cone, because a plane not through the vertex would project to a plane contained in a smooth cubic surface. Independent GF(4) line enumeration found exactly 45 projective points, 27 lines, 15 Frobenius-fixed lines and 6 nontrivial pairs, checked against all 15 specialized pair-partition planes; geometric completeness additionally uses the classical 27-lines theorem, not finite-field sampling. The normal-bundle map for each cone plane is a pair of base-point-free binary quadratics with no linear syzygy, giving reduced isolated Hilbert points. The generic 15 pairing planes are reduced. Thus different finite fiber lengths imply nonflatness. The Gauss map on the base is its projective Frobenius, degree 2^2=4, not a finite-degree Gauss map of the cone.
